body.x: Daegu Metropolitan City held the official opening ceremony for the Future Innovation Tech Expo 2026 (FIX 2026) at EXCO on Wednesday, October 21, at 10:30 AM. Organized under the theme “AI, beyond Tech into reality,” the four-day industrial exhibition brought together international industry executives, technology developers, and policymakers to showcase how artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and advanced robotics are actively transitioning into real-world production environments and daily consumer life.

body.x: The opening ceremony welcomed approximately 100 distinguished dignitaries representing national government bodies, regional administration, academia, and industry leadership. Key attendees included Kyung-ho Choo, Mayor of Daegu Metropolitan City; Yong-seok Kim, President of the Metropolitan Area Transport Commission; Jung-Woo Ha, Vice Chairman of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy Committee; In-hwan Lim, Chairman of the Daegu Metropolitan Council; Jae-jun Woo, Representative; Eun-hee Kang, Superintendent of the Daegu Metropolitan Office of Education; Seok Cho, Vice Chairman of HD Hyundai; Wansoo Kim, President and CEO of HD Hyundai Robotics; Youngmin Kwon, CEO of Doosan Robotics; Hang-soo Lee, Vice President of Hyundai Motor Group; Brian McMurray, President of General Motors Technical Center Korea (GMTCK); and Kyujin Cho, Professor at Seoul National University.

Following the formal ceremony, VIP delegations participated in a curated exhibition floor tour that covered major technology hubs throughout the convention center. The tour began at the Urban Air Mobility (UAM) Special Pavilion, featuring the commercial airframe developed by Germany’s Volocopter, before proceeding to Hyundai Motor Company’s exhibition of an unmanned firefighting robot and its proprietary autonomous driving AI platform, ATRIA AI. The delegation also reviewed demonstrations of the autonomous delivery vehicle RoboVan presented by NT1, Neolix’s domestic operating partner in Korea, alongside dual-arm industrial collaborative robots from HD Hyundai Robotics, the CES 2026 Best of Innovation Award-winning Scan&Go system by Doosan Robotics, and cloud management infrastructure from MegazoneCloud.

body.cap: Kyung-ho Choo, Mayor of Daegu Metropolitan City, listened to the description from the representative of Volocopter inside its UAM on display | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The opening-day conference program featured afternoon keynote presentations by prominent domestic and international scholars and executives. Kyujin Cho, a globally recognized robotics authority and Professor at Seoul National University, opened the session with a keynote titled “The Age of Discovery for Physical AI Robots.” Subsequent addresses were delivered by Brian McMurray, President of GMTCK; Professor Xiaoxiao Shaun Li of the Vector Institute, who presented research on multimodal AI architectures; and Francesco Ferro, CEO of European humanoid robotics developer PAL Robotics.

Beyond heavy industrial automation, FIX 2026 placed significant emphasis on applied AI and robotics designed to solve real-world municipal, medical, and commercial challenges. Highlights included an AI-driven unmanned robotic convenience store platform, specialized municipal odor mitigation systems, and a high-precision robotic navigation platform engineered for orthopedic fracture surgeries.

The event also offered extensive interactive and participatory programs for attendees, featuring public boarding simulations of Volocopter’s UAM airframe, tactical drone piloting challenges, generative AI interactive sessions at the KT AI Station, automated F&B service robotics, and electric vehicle test-drive circuits. Open to visitors through Saturday, October 24, the expo operated with dedicated circular shuttle services linking Dongdaegu Station and EXCO. Daegu Mayor Kyung-ho Choo noted that FIX 2026 provides a direct look at the industrial restructuring driven by AI convergence, affirming that the city will continue to accelerate the AI transformation of its primary industries to ensure technological progress translates into long-term economic development.
